analysis.title: Weekly Automotive Pit Stop: Supplier conference, Mobility Global takeaways
key_insights: Mobility Global forecasts US sales flat YoY in 2027 at 16.1mm units and sees downside risk as the consumer looks stretched, with loan payments approaching $800/month.

North America model launches accelerate to about 30 in 2028, about 60 in 2029 and about 48 in 2030, versus the roughly 40 peak in 2006. Programs have been pushed out repeatedly during the EV strategy reset, and delays or extensions of current programs are a risk.

Mobility Global sees a renewed long-term USMCA deal as unlikely for at least another year and assumes existing tariffs largely stay in place, with limited political appetite for a rollback even under a different administration.
Mobility Global cut China production forecasts by 500K units in 2026 and 1.6mm units in 2027. Chinese domestic sales are down 21.5% this year.

Chinese OEM entry into the US looks unlikely over the next few years, but Chinese OEM and supply-chain presence in Mexico is growing rapidly. The EU import cap on Chinese hybrids in 2027 is likely to push Chinese OEMs toward local production in Europe, where they could reach 24% of capacity by 2033.
DRAM supply and price pressure is broadening to PCBs and legacy-node chips, adding $350-400 of cost per vehicle in 2027.

The MEMA supplier conference tone was relatively cautious, with concerns about cost inflation, competition from Chinese brands and pricing pressure on suppliers with operations in China. Attendees mostly agreed Chinese vehicles will not enter the US near term but that eventual entry is inevitable and share gains could be rapid.
NHTSA is updating safety standards for vehicles designed without human drivers and is targeting a proposal within a year.

BofA estimates Tesla's Texas robotaxi fleet at 1,507 vehicles as of 11/19, up 204 (+16%) WoW and up 649 (+76%) since 10/23, ahead of Waymo's 1,328 for the first time. Cybercab added 200 units to reach 773, or 51.3% of the fleet, against 4 added Model Ys.

Tesla priced a personal-use Cybercab at $29,990 with a $299 monthly Autonomy Subscription. Musk said the fee is too high and should be closer to the roughly $115 FSD and connectivity cost on other models. BofA sees personal use as early, with robotaxi the primary near-term focus.

October US light vehicle sales fell 0.8% YoY on a selling-day-adjusted basis to a 15.5mm SAAR, down from 16.0mm in September. This was below BofA's mid-month estimate of 15.9mm and Bloomberg consensus of 15.8mm. YTD SAAR is 16.0mm versus 16.3mm in FY25.

BofA attributes the sequential sales decline to elevated gas prices and re-accelerating inflation on a constrained affordability backdrop. Demand has held up YTD as wealthier buyers take a growing share and an aging fleet adds replacement demand.
US inventory rose 114k units MoM to 2.71mm in October, or 57 days' supply against a 5-year average of 51. Ford (83 days) and Stellantis (99 days) are elevated relative to GM (73 days).

Average transaction prices rose 2.1% YoY to $51,109 in October (+1.3% MoM, per Kelley Blue Book). Incentives rose 7.8% YoY and 4.0% MoM, at 6.8% of ATP versus about 10% in 2019. Hybrid demand is up 20% YoY and EV demand about +1.5% YoY.
BofA estimates raw material cost per vehicle rose 2% MoM in October to $4,967, up 35% YoY. Ford and GM expect $2.0bn and about $1.25bn (midpoint) of incremental commodity headwinds, respectively.

BofA analysis shows a 10%+ sequential rise in monthly gas prices correlates with a 90bps reduction in the mix of larger vehicle purchases (SUVs, trucks, vans) over the following 6 months. US retail gas is $3.95 and diesel $5.94, up 28.4% and 55.9% since the Iran conflict.
Tesla China wholesale volume rose for the 11th straight month to 68k in October (+10% YoY). Tesla Korea sales were 9.1k in October (+111% YoY, -26% MoM). Tesla US October sales were -6.3% YoY.
In the EU, EFTA and UK, Chinese brands rose 75.3% YoY in September and reached 16.0% share, versus 10.0% a year earlier. BEV registrations rose 59.9% YoY and reached 30.5% share.
China passenger car retail sales fell 26.7% YoY and BEV sales fell 5.2% YoY in October.

market_movers.rationale: The Texas robotaxi fleet passed Waymo's, with Cybercab now 51.3% of the fleet. Valuation is a sum-of-the-parts analysis.
Ford October US sales were -5.1% YoY and inventory is elevated at 83 days' supply. Ford expects $2.0bn of commodity headwinds.
GM gained 26bps of US share MoM. It expects about $1.25bn of commodity headwinds and carries lean inventory at 73 days.
Valuation is a premium EV/EBITDA multiple on exposure to content-driven growth.
8.0x P/E on 2027 estimates, with a high-quality OEM portfolio and a strong parts and services business.
9.0x P/E on 2027 EPS, supported by the 2026 off-lease wave and a share repurchase pace ahead of peers.
8.1x EV/EBITDA on 2027 estimates, with the 2027 entrance into the data center market as a longer-term tailwind.
17.9x P/E on FY2028 estimates, a premium to the 5-year average of 15.5x, justified by recent operational execution.
8.0x P/E on 2027 EPS, with consistent same-store sales outperformance in parts and services and F&I.
10.2x P/E on 2027 estimates, backed by a track record of earnings and M&A execution.
5.3x EV/EBITDA on 2027 estimates, reflecting growth over market and margin expansion.
13.2x P/E on 2027 estimates, a premium to the dealer average, on a premium brand portfolio and a strong parts and services business.
5.25x EV/EBITDA on 2027 estimates. Seating share gains partly offset below-market growth in e-systems.
13x-14x adjusted EV/EBITDA on 2027 estimates, with incoming off-lease returns as a multi-year supply tailwind.
3.1x EV/EBITDA on 2028 estimates. Europe is weak and contract extensions could prolong unprofitable metal contracts.
3.6x EV/EBITDA on 2027 estimates, with the company seen as a beneficiary of a more favorable backdrop for ICE vehicles.
1.6x EV/Sales on 2027 estimates, at the low end of its historical range given a tougher EV regulatory backdrop and slower adoption.
1.7x EV/Sales on 2027 estimates, at the low end of its historical range given a tougher EV regulatory backdrop and slower adoption.

sector_views.rationale: US demand is holding up on wealthier buyers and replacement demand. Affordability is stretched, inventory is rising, and raw material and DRAM costs are inflating.
The MEMA conference tone was cautious on cost inflation, Chinese competition and pricing pressure. Aptiv, BorgWarner and Magna are rated Buy, and Adient and Dauch Underperform.
Most covered dealers are rated Buy (ABG, AN, GPI, LAD, SAH, KMX). Used vehicle values are up and off-lease supply is expected to rise.

tension_points.bull_case: Wealthier consumers are a growing share of new vehicle buyers, an aging fleet is adding pent-up replacement demand, and YTD SAAR is 16.0mm.
tension_points.bear_case: October SAAR fell to 15.5mm, below estimates. Loan payments are approaching $800/month, gas prices are elevated, and Mobility Global sees downside risk to its flat 2027 forecast.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Gasoline rising 10%+ sequentially, which BofA's analysis ties to a 90bps drop in larger-vehicle mix and weaker SAAR over the following 6 months.
